chunks: He said: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Umar al-Ji'abi reported from Abul Abbas Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Saeed, who reported from Abdullah ibn Ahmad ibn Mustawrad, who reported from Muhammad ibn Munir, who reported from Ishaq ibn Wazir, who reported from Muhammad ibn al-Fudhayl ibn Ata, the client of Muzaynah, who reported from Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them), from his father, that Muhammad ibn Ali, Ibn al-Hanafiyyah (may God be pleased with him) said:
The standard of the army was with me on the day of the Battle of the Camel, and the worst casualties were among the Banu Dabbah.

When the people were defeated, Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him), accompanied by Ammar ibn Yasir and Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr (may God be pleased with them), came to the howdah, which looked like the spikes of a porcupine because of the arrows in it. He struck it with a stick and said:

'Well, O Humayra! You wanted to kill me just as you killed the son of Affan?! Is this what God commanded you, or what the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his family, entrusted to you?' She said: 'You have conquered, so be forgiving.' Then he (peace be upon him) said to Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr:

'Check whether any weapon reached her.' He found her safe; nothing had reached her except an arrow that had torn her garment and scratched her insignificantly. Then Ibn Abi Bakr said: 'O Commander of the Faithful, she is safe from weapons except for an arrow that reached her clothing and scratched her a little.'

Then Ali (peace be upon him) said: 'Convey her and lodge her in the house of the two sons of Khalaf al-Khuzai.' Then he ordered his announcer, who proclaimed: 'No wounded person shall be killed, no one fleeing shall be pursued, and whoever shuts his door is safe.'

key_terms.اللواء: The military standard or banner, symbolizing command authority in battle
key_terms.الهودج: Howdah — a litter or covered seat mounted on a camel, in which Aisha rode during the battle
key_terms.حميراء: Humayra — a diminutive form of the word for 'red', a nickname for Aisha
key_terms.فاسجح: Be forgiving/lenient — an Arabic expression urging clemency after victory
key_terms.يدفف: To deliver a coup de grâce or finish off a wounded person on the battlefield

ai.seo_question: What happened after the Battle of the Camel between Imam Ali and Aisha?
ai.summary: Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah recounts events after the Battle of the Camel (36 AH/656 CE), where Imam Ali approached Aisha's howdah after his forces prevailed. After rebuking her for her role in the conflict and comparing it to the instigation against Uthman, Ali showed mercy by ensuring her safety, ordering her housed respectfully, and issuing a general amnesty forbidding the killing of the wounded and pursuit of the fleeing.

en.mulla-asgharali-m-m-jaffer: 8. He said: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Umar al-Ji’abi reported from Abul Abbas Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Saeed, who reported from Abdullah ibn Ahmad ibn Mustawrad, who reported from Muhammad ibn Munir, who reported from Ishaq ibn Wazir, who reported from Muhammad ibn al-Fudhail ibn Ata, the client of Mazeenah, who reported from Ja’far ibn Muhammad (as), from his father, who reported that Muhammad ibn ‘Ali, Ibn Hanafiyya said:
"The standard of the army on the day of the battle of Jamal was with me, and the worst casualties were suffered by Bani Zabbah.

When the people retreated, Amirul Mu’mineen (as), accompanied by Ammar ibn Yasir and Muhammad ibn Abu Bakr, may Allah bless them with His Pleasure - came to the howdah (of Aisha) which looked like the spike of a porcupine because of the arrows which had pierced it, and he hit it with his stick and said:

’O, Humayra, you wanted to kill me the way you killed the son of Affan (i.e. Uthman). Is this what Allah has commanded you? Or is this the pledge which the Prophet, peace be upon him and his progeny, took from you?’ She said: ’You have conquered, so be forgiving.’ Then he (i.e. ‘Ali {AS}) said to Muhammad ibn Abu Bakr:

’Find out if she has been hit with any weapon.’ He found her safe, except for an arrow, which had pierced her attire, and grazed her a little. So Ibn Abi Bakr said: ’O Amirul Mu’mineen, She is safe, except for an arrow, which has struck her clothes and bruised her a bit.’

So ‘Ali said: ’Convey her to the house of the two sons of Khalaf al-Khuzai.’ And then he ordered an announcer to announce: The wounded should not be killed, and those running away should not be pursued. And whoever shuts his door, he will be in peace."
